svg.text: LlamaIndex + TruLens (TruEra) — basic vs advanced retrieval, benchmarked with the RAG triad
Essence: A basic RAG pipeline runs in three stages — ingestion, retrieval, and
synthesis. Two advanced retrieval methods — sentence-window and auto-merging — add
richer context at answer time. TruLens scores every version on the RAG triad to benchmark.
🧱 The basic RAG pipeline — three stages
Ingestion: load documents, split into chunks, embed each chunk, store the vectors in an index.
Retrieval: embed the user query, then fetch the top-K chunks most similar to it.
Synthesis: place those chunks and the query into the LLM prompt to write the final answer.
⚙️ Set up the baseline with LlamaIndex + TruLens
We build a simple LlamaIndex app over one PDF (Andrew Ng's "How to Build a Career in AI").
The 41 PDF pages are merged into one document — this helps the advanced retrievers blend
That single from_documents call chunks, embeds (BGE-small), and indexes — all in one step.
TruLens uses an LLM as a judge to score each answer with three pairwise checks between
the query, the retrieved context, and the response. High on all three = low hallucination.
Baseline result: answer relevance and groundedness are already high, but context relevance is
low (0.26). That weak score is the target the two advanced retrievers try to fix.
Embed and retrieve single sentences (very granular matching). After a sentence is found,
replace it with a window of the sentences around it before sending to the LLM.
So you match precisely, but give the LLM more context to answer well.
Match on one sentence (S3), then expand to its surrounding window before synthesis.
Build a hierarchy: large parent nodes, each split into several smaller child nodes.
Retrieve on the small children. If a parent has most of its children retrieved, merge them
and hand the LLM the whole parent instead — one clean, complete block of text.
The four children together hold the same text as their parent, so merging loses nothing.
📊 Results — three engines on the RAG triad
Auto-merging wins: groundedness 1.00 and context relevance 0.44, up from 0.80 / 0.26.
Answer relevance stays high for all three (~0.93) — it was never the problem.
Sentence-window lands in the middle: groundedness 0.88, context relevance 0.37.
Cost drops too: auto-merging $0.0008 vs baseline $0.0029 per run; latency ~2.2s for all.
• TruEra (makers of TruLens) was acquired by Snowflake in 2024; TruLens stays open source.
• TruLens now integrates with Snowflake Cortex and modern agent frameworks, not just RAG.
• LlamaIndex moved imports to llama_index.core; gpt-3.5-turbo is legacy — prefer newer models.
• The RAG triad (context relevance, groundedness, answer relevance) is still the standard eval.
Better retrieval — not a bigger model — fixed the weak metric. Give the LLM the right,
complete context (windowed or merged) and both grounding and cost improve together.
Always benchmark each change against a baseline using the same evaluation triad.
